title: Callback patterns and error-first conventions
hook: Before Promises dominated, Node standardized on callbacks with the error as the first argument. That convention still appears in fs, legacy APIs, and interview questions about control flow and error propagation.

blocks.text: A **callback** is a function passed to another function to run later — on I/O completion, timer fire, or user click. Node's **error-first callback** signature is `(err, result) => void`: if `err` is truthy, treat it as failure; otherwise use `result`. Synchronous callbacks run immediately; asynchronous callbacks run on a later **event loop** turn. **Higher-order functions** like `array.map(cb)` use the same idea synchronously.

entries.plainDefinition: Node convention: first parameter is Error or null, second is success payload.
Function representing 'what to do next' after async work — callback or .then handler.
Deep nesting when each async step needs the next callback inline.
entries.example: Three nested fs.readFile calls — hard to read and handle errors.

entries.plainDefinition: Wraps error-first callback API into a function returning Promise.

blocks.text: You still maintain code using `fs.readFile`, database drivers with callback modes, and third-party libs from the 2010s. Interviews test whether you know **why** `(err, data)` order exists and how to **promisify**, not just `async/await`. C# uses `Action<T>` and `Task` continuations — error-first is Node-specific ergonomics, not a language feature.

blocks.title: Interview trap: throw inside callback
blocks.body: Throwing in an async callback does not become a rejected Promise unless wrapped — it becomes an uncaught exception on the next tick. Always pass errors via err first or wrap with Promise.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: I/O completes
items.body: Lib invokes callback on thread pool / libuv thread, marshaled to JS thread.

items.title: Check err
items.body: if (err) handle and return — do not touch result.

items.title: Use result
items.body: Continue logic or call next callback in chain.

diagram.title: Error-first callback decision
diagram.source:
flowchart TD
  A[API invokes callback] --> B{err truthy?}
  B -->|yes| C[Handle error path]
  B -->|no| D[Use result]
  C --> E[Return early]
  D --> F[Next step]

snippet.label: Classic error-first API
snippet.explanation: Early return on err — never JSON.parse when read failed. err.code distinguishes ENOENT vs EACCES.

snippet.label: Manual promisify
snippet.explanation: Maps err to reject, result to resolve — foundation of util.promisify and how Promise bridges callbacks.

snippet.label: C# Task instead of error-first
snippet.explanation: C# uses exceptions + Task — no err-first parameter. Node historically avoided throw across async C++ boundary.

snippet.label: Failure mode: forgotten err check
snippet.explanation: Most common callback bug in code review — silent undefined then secondary crash.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Calling callback twice (success then error). Mixing return value with callback style. Forgetting err check. Throwing instead of passing err in library code you author.

blocks.text: When authoring callback APIs: document error codes, never invoke callback more than once, and support both callback and Promise if you must (dual API — avoid if greenfield). Use `util.callbackify` sparingly for legacy interop. In production migrate hot paths to promises with fs.promises, pg native promise driver, etc.

blocks.title: Tradeoffs at senior level
rows: No single err callback per op

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Not knowing err-first parameter order. Claiming throw in async fs callback becomes Promise reject automatically. Cannot write manual promisify or explain why Node chose err-first.

interviewTakeaways: Node error-first: (err, result) — check err before using result.
Throw in async callback ≠ rejected Promise unless wrapped.
promisify maps err→reject for migration to async/await.
60s: Callbacks are continuations. Node err-first avoids exceptions across libuv. C# uses Task exceptions. Always guard err; promisify for legacy; prefer fs.promises.
Follow-up: implement promisify handling APIs where callback is not last argument.
commonPitfalls: Skipping err check and operating on undefined result.
Invoking the same callback twice on retry logic.
Strong answer: err-first convention, promisify pattern, C# Task contrast, migrate to promises.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Node @types use typed err as NodeJS.ErrnoException | null — mirrors error-first at compile time.
Official bridge from callbacks to Promises — understand before relying on async/await sugar.
